players.product: intismeran autogene (V940/mRNA-4157) individualized neoantigen therapy, jointly developed with Merck

quarterly_data.signal: President Stephen Hoge: Moderna is still targeting break even in 2028, based on the strength of its infectious disease vaccines business; the intismeran investments of the last few years (a large book of work with partner Merck, including nine ongoing clinical trials) are baked into that target, and further intismeran investments (monotherapy, earlier-stage and stage 1 disease) will be made only where the data directs. Guidance for now is up to 10% growth on the top line for this year, which he called the right mental model while not wanting to raise expectations further; the vaccine portfolio needs no additional commercial or manufacturing infrastructure.
quarterly_data.figure: break even still targeted for 2028; 2026 top-line growth guidance up to 10% retained

quarterly_data.signal: Hoge on intismeran manufacturing and launch capacity: Moderna has treated about 3,000 patients (close to 1,500 to 2,000 in the last 18 months alone) across its nine global trials in 42 countries, all supplied from a purpose-built, highly automated manufacturing system built in Marlborough, which he says already operates at commercial scale. The facility can supply launch: one of seven suites ('ballrooms') is built out, all technology is licensed and in place, and with about 12 months of lead time capacity can be taken up another sevenfold; the company does not think it needs suite 2 for launch while still supporting the clinical trials, and would discuss a second facility only if demand really takes off. He said the capability, built in 2023, 2024 and 2025, is now paid for.
quarterly_data.figure: about 3,000 patients treated (1,500 to 2,000 in the last 18 months) in 42 countries; suite 1 of 7 built out; capacity can rise another sevenfold with about 12 months of lead time; suite 2 not needed for launch

quarterly_data.signal: Hoge on the intismeran (with Merck) program: the positive phase III adjuvant melanoma interim analysis was a statistically significant and clinically meaningful result against KEYTRUDA, which he called the first time anybody has achieved that kind of benefit over KEYTRUDA in the adjuvant melanoma setting (company claim); the full data will be shared at an upcoming medical meeting. The adjuvant renal cell carcinoma and muscle-invasive bladder cancer phase II studies are fully enrolled and event-driven, and the non-muscle invasive bladder cancer monotherapy phase II is not yet fully enrolled; all three randomize approximately 300 patients one-to-one against standard of care (KEYTRUDA in the adjuvant RCC and MIBC studies) and could read out in the near term. The lung program comprises three randomized phase IIIs being enrolled (event-driven) plus a large randomized phase II in frontline metastatic disease; Moderna and Merck have set up the program to deliver waves of clinical data every 6 months.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 300 patients randomized one-to-one in each of the RCC, MIBC and NMIBC studies; three randomized phase IIIs in lung cancer

quarterly_data.signal: Hoge on intismeran regulation and economics: if melanoma is approved, the CMC / manufacturing and safety modules of the BLA are common across indications, so statistically significant phase II studies such as RCC and MIBC can and should be registrational. Because software is part of the drug, Moderna has been working closely with the FDA, EMA and other regulators to define which neoantigen-selection software updates are a major change requiring an sBLA versus a prior approval supplement. Pricing is premature (the company will price to value after the data and payer discussions); management is pretty confident about the margin profile and hopes margins over time are very competitive with other complex biologics, not cell therapy, since the manufacturing technology and chemical matter are essentially the same across patients. Retreatment with a new product reflecting a relapsed tumor is a hypothesis with no data yet.

Hoge on vaccines: with five product approvals (COVID, flu, RSV, the first combination product and second-generation COVID mNEXSPIKE), Moderna can contract at portfolio level - internationally through strategic partnerships with the U.K., Canada, Australia and other governments coming online, offering flexibility across the portfolio, and in the U.S. with healthcare systems and pharmacies, getting a first taste of this year. In Europe this year Moderna is launching the flu/COVID combination vaccine (one shot). He described U.S.-approved flu vaccine mFLUSIVA as the first enhanced-efficacy flu vaccine for seniors without egg-based manufacturing (company claim), noting that 95% of flu vaccines are currently made in eggs.
quarterly_data.figure: five product approvals; flu/COVID combination launching in Europe this year
